value.body: A three-year surgical postgraduate degree in eye care after MBBS. Training covers diagnosis and treatment of eye disease, refraction and surgery — cataract surgery first, with exposure to glaucoma, retina, cornea, squint and oculoplastics. DNB Ophthalmology (NBEMS) is a parallel route of the same length.

items.note: All postgraduate ophthalmology programmes, not only MS; about 69% are women

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An MBBS with completed internship and registration, then NEET-PG. 50% of seats in government medical colleges, plus deemed and central university seats, are allotted through all-India counselling by the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC); the rest go through state counselling.

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the work is outpatient clinics and planned surgery, with generally fewer night emergencies than many surgical specialties.
Surgical skill builds with case volume, so the number of surgeries a residency offers matters.
Further sub-specialisation (retina, cornea, glaucoma and others) is usually through fellowships.
Setting up an independent eye practice needs costly equipment; many begin in eye hospitals.
